issues.display_title: Issue #3488: Epic: GoThru App-to-App Data Exchange Integration
issues.main_description_html:
Target Project: GoThru app backends that participate in cross-app data exchange, including Villume, Dashboard, Panorra, and future GoThru services.
PIC (Person In Charge): Backend lead for each participating app, with DevOps support for Keycloak configuration.
Status: TODO

1. Overview

Implement a Keycloak-based service account architecture that allows one GoThru application to securely request business data from another GoThru application on behalf of an already-authenticated user.

The frontend must not call another GoThru app directly. The user-facing app backend acts as the requestor/proxy, obtains a Keycloak service account token, calls the provider app's internal API, normalizes the response, and returns it to its own frontend.

2. Goals

  • Allow backend-to-backend GoThru service calls using Keycloak client_credentials service account tokens.
  • Use the Keycloak user UUID (sub) as the only cross-app user identifier.
  • Keep credentials and identity in Keycloak, while each app keeps its own business data.
  • Support users who have not previously logged into the provider app through deterministic JIT provisioning.
  • Return graceful empty states for users with no provider-side data.

3. Non-Goals

  • Do not expose provider internal APIs directly to frontend applications.
  • Do not use local numeric user IDs across applications.
  • Do not share user passwords, local sessions, or frontend access tokens between apps.
  • Do not implement broad internal access just because a caller is a GoThru app; authorization must remain route-aware.

4. Core Identity Contract

  • Keycloak is the source of truth for identity credentials and the universal user UUID.
  • Every participating app must persist a stable mapping from local user/profile record to Keycloak sub.
  • Cross-app requests must pass the Keycloak UUID, not a local database ID.
  • Provider apps must enforce uniqueness for Keycloak UUID mappings.

5. Supported User/Data Scenarios

Provider internal endpoints must handle these cases consistently:

  1. User exists in provider and data exists

    • Provider finds the local user by Keycloak UUID.
    • Provider returns 200 OK with the data payload.

  2. User exists in provider but data does not exist

    • Provider finds the local user.
    • Provider returns 200 OK with an empty array [].
    • This must not be treated as an error.

  3. User does not exist in provider

    • Provider receives a valid Keycloak UUID it has never seen before.
    • Provider performs JIT provisioning by creating a minimal local user/profile record linked to that Keycloak UUID.
    • Provider returns 200 OK with an empty array [].
    • The JIT operation must be idempotent and safe under concurrent duplicate requests.

6. Security Contract

  • Requestor apps obtain service account tokens from Keycloak using grant_type=client_credentials.
  • Provider internal routes must verify incoming bearer tokens using Keycloak JWKS.
  • Provider validation must check:
    • JWT signature.
    • iss matches the configured Keycloak realm issuer.
    • exp and nbf are valid, with a small configured clock skew.
    • aud or equivalent accepted audience matches the provider/internal API contract.
    • azp or client_id identifies an allowed calling app.
    • JWT algorithm is restricted to expected asymmetric algorithms, such as RS256, based on the realm configuration.
  • Authorization must be allowlist-based and route-aware. A caller allowed for one internal endpoint is not automatically allowed for every internal endpoint.
  • Unknown, expired, malformed, or unauthorized tokens must be rejected before business logic runs.

7. Provider API Contract

Each provider app must create dedicated internal routes under a clearly separated route group, for example:

GET /api/internal/users/{keycloak_uuid}/assets
Authorization: Bearer <keycloak-service-token>

For list-style asset endpoints:

  • 200 OK with an array payload when the request is valid.
  • 200 OK with [] when the user is known but has no data.
  • 200 OK with [] after successful JIT provisioning for an unknown user.
  • 401 Unauthorized when the bearer token is missing or invalid.
  • 403 Forbidden when the caller app is authenticated but not allowed for the endpoint.
  • 400 Bad Request when the Keycloak UUID format is invalid.
  • 5xx only for real infrastructure or unexpected server failures.

If pagination, filtering, or a response envelope is needed, it must be documented in the provider subtask before implementation starts.

8. Requestor Backend Contract

Requestor apps must:

  • Store and read the user's Keycloak UUID from the local user/session identity mapping.
  • Fetch and cache Keycloak service account tokens.
  • Respect token expires_in and refresh before expiry.
  • Use an internal HTTP client wrapper that injects Authorization: Bearer <service-token>.
  • Pass the user's Keycloak UUID in the provider URL or request body according to the provider API contract.
  • Normalize provider responses before returning them to the frontend.
  • Treat provider [] responses as valid empty states, not failures.

9. Frontend Handling

Frontend apps continue to call only their own backend using the local app authentication/session.

The frontend must not know:

  • Keycloak service account credentials.
  • Provider internal API URLs.
  • Provider service tokens.

When the backend returns an empty array for provider assets, the frontend should show a friendly empty state such as:

You don't have any assets in GoThru Dashboard yet.

10. Sample Seamless Integration UI Flow

This epic should support a seamless cross-app data exchange view where a user can select existing assets from another GoThru product without signing in again or understanding the backend service-token exchange.

Example flow: a user creates a new post in Panorra and chooses to embed a trail or tour from Tourmkr.

  1. Select provider source

    • The UI shows available source platforms, such as Tourmkr and Google Street View.
    • When the user chooses Select from my Tourmkr, the frontend calls only the Panorra backend using the user's local Panorra session.
    • The frontend does not call Tourmkr directly.

  2. Open provider asset picker

    • The UI opens a modal or sheet titled Select from my Tourmkr.
    • Tabs separate asset types, for example Trails and Tours.
    • Search and selection controls are local UI concerns, backed by the normalized response from the requestor backend.

  3. Show user-context-aware loading

    • While Panorra backend fetches Tourmkr data, the UI shows a loading state such as Loading your Tourmkr data....
    • The loading state may show the currently signed-in user identity for confidence, using local/session profile data.
    • The UI must not expose service account details, provider API URLs, access tokens, or internal error traces.

  4. Data loaded: user exists and assets exist

    • If Tourmkr returns assets, the UI lists trails/tours with enough metadata for selection, such as title, thumbnail, distance, and location.
    • The user can select one or more supported assets and continue.
    • This corresponds to backend use case 1: provider user exists and data exists.

  5. Empty state: user exists but no assets

    • If Tourmkr returns 200 OK with [], the UI shows a friendly empty state.
    • The empty state should offer useful next actions, such as Create on Tourmkr or Add link instead.
    • This corresponds to backend use case 2: provider user exists but data does not exist.

  6. Empty state: provider user is new

    • If Tourmkr does not know the Keycloak UUID yet, the backend performs JIT provisioning and returns 200 OK with [].
    • The UI should show the same empty state as use case 2.
    • The user should not see an error just because the provider-side profile was created on demand.

UI/Backend Contract for This Flow

  • The requestor backend owns service-token fetching, provider calls, and response normalization.
  • The frontend receives a normal authenticated response from its own backend.
  • A returned empty array means a valid empty state, not a failed integration.
  • Provider auth failures should produce a controlled frontend error state, not a crash.
  • Backend responses should include enough normalized fields for the picker UI to render thumbnails, names, asset type, and provider IDs.
  • The picker should remain usable when the provider is slow by showing loading, retry, and empty states clearly.

11. Operational Requirements

  • Add required Keycloak settings and environment variables to each participating app.
  • Document local, staging, and production configuration differences.
  • Store secrets only in approved secret storage or environment configuration, never in source control.
  • Add structured logs for requestor calls, provider authentication failures, JIT provisioning events, and provider response status.
  • Avoid logging tokens, refresh tokens, client secrets, or full personally identifiable user payloads.
  • Add tests for token caching, JWT verification, authorization failures, empty data, existing users, and JIT provisioning.

12. Architecture Diagram

sequenceDiagram
    participant FE as Frontend (Panorra UI)
    participant AppA as Requestor Backend (Panorra)
    participant KC as Keycloak (SSO)
    participant AppB as Provider Backend (Tourmkr)

    Note over FE,AppA: User is already logged into Panorra locally
    FE->>AppA: 1. Get my Tourmkr trails/tours using local Panorra auth

    rect rgb(30, 40, 50)
        Note over AppA,KC: Panorra acts as a service account client
        AppA->>KC: 2. Request service token using client_credentials
        KC-->>AppA: 3. Return Keycloak JWT service token
    end

    AppA->>AppA: 4. Load user's Keycloak UUID (sub) from Panorra user mapping

    rect rgb(30, 50, 40)
        Note over AppA,AppB: Panorra securely calls Tourmkr
        AppA->>AppB: 5. GET /api/internal/users/{uuid}/assets with bearer service token
    end

    AppB->>AppB: 6. Verify JWT using cached JWKS
    AppB->>AppB: 7. Validate issuer, audience, expiry, and Panorra caller allowlist
    AppB->>AppB: 8. Find or JIT-provision Tourmkr user by Keycloak UUID
    AppB->>AppB: 9. Load user's Tourmkr trails/tours

    AppB-->>AppA: 10. Return trails/tours array or []
    AppA-->>FE: 11. Return normalized picker response to Panorra UI
Loading

13. Definition of Done

  • All participating apps have Keycloak service account configuration documented.
  • Requestor apps can fetch, cache, and use service account tokens.
  • Provider apps expose protected internal routes under a dedicated route group.
  • Provider apps verify JWT signature, issuer, expiry, audience, and caller identity.
  • Provider authorization uses an explicit app/route allowlist.
  • Keycloak UUID is persisted and used as the cross-app user identifier.
  • Unknown provider-side users are JIT-provisioned idempotently.
  • Existing/no-data/unknown-user scenarios all return the expected 200 OK payloads.
  • Frontend-facing backend responses support a friendly empty state.
  • The sample provider asset picker flow can render loading, data-loaded, empty, retry, and controlled-error states.
  • Unit or integration tests cover the success, empty, unauthorized, forbidden, invalid UUID, and JIT paths.
  • Secrets are excluded from source control and reflected only as placeholders in example env files.

14. Dedicated Subtasks

  • #10
  • #11
  • #12
  • #13

issues.display_title: Issue #3463: [Add Post] Integrate API Get Virtual Tour GoThru List Tours
issues.main_description_html:
Result BE

  • GoThruMedia/panorra-api-go#577

API Usage & Examples (Frontend Guide)

Endpoint

GET /gothru/virtual-tours

Frontend simply calls this Panorra endpoint with the standard Panorra user Bearer token. Frontend does not need to send user_id or deal with Keycloak/GoThru directly.

Headers

Authorization: Bearer <panorra_token>
Accept: application/json

Query Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
search string No - Filter by tour name (tour_name) or tour key (tour_key)
page int No 1 Page number (min: 1)
per_page int No 20 Number of items per page (min: 1, max: 100)

Request Examples

1. Default (Page 1, 20 items)

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/gothru/virtual-tours" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <panorra_user_token>" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

2. With Search and Pagination

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/gothru/virtual-tours?search=Gym&page=2&per_page=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <panorra_user_token>" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response Examples

1. 200 OK — Tours Found

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": [
    {
      "tour_id": 820508,
      "cdn": "0",
      "tour_key": "u1NXOiVK",
      "1_cid": "583554146763372625",
      "moderation_id": 3591071,
      "tour_name": "Gym Fit Forme",
      "creation_date": "2026-09-28 05:00:05",
      "last_update": "2026-09-28 05:00:05",
      "lat": "45.6466825",
      "lng": "-73.5684739",
      "vr": "1",
      "deactivated": "0"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 1,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total_pages": 1
  }
}

2. 200 OK — No Tours / Empty State

Note: This is a valid empty state, not an error. Display a user-friendly empty state in the UI.

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": [],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total_pages": 0
  }
}

3. 404 Not Found — Account Not Linked to GoThru

User has no entry in the user_keycloak_link table.

{
  "statusCode": 404,
  "data": {
    "message": "Keycloak account is not linked for this user"
  }
}

4. 401 Unauthorized — Session Expired / Invalid Token

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "message": "Unauthorized"
  }
}

5. 502 Bad Gateway — GoThru Service Down or Unreachable

{
  "statusCode": 502,
  "data": {
    "message": "Unable to connect to GoThru service"
  }
}

Frontend Integration Guide

Endpoint

Headers

Header Value Description

Query Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description

Response Model (TypeScript)

export interface VirtualTourItem {
  tour_key: string;       // E.g. "PWHsBHrg"
  name: string;           // E.g. "Spirit Mountain Recreation Area"
  lat: number;            // E.g. 46.717
  lng: number;            // E.g. -92.2151
  cid: string;            // Google CID (from 1_cid)

    per_page: number;
    total_pages: number;

Validation Specification

Rule Draft Mode Publish Mode Error Response Input
JSON syntax Valid JSON required Valid JSON required trail
Points count Min 1 point Min 1 point (no upper cap) trail.points
Point URL https://tourmkr.com/F1... or G1... Same trail.points[i].url
URL uniqueness No duplicate URLs across points No duplicate URLs trail.points[i].url
Prefix consistency All F1 or all G1 for entire trail Same trail.points[i].url
Lat & Lng Numbers required Numbers required trail.points[i].url
Point name Optional Required, max 100 characters trail.points[i].name
Height (height_m) Optional (default 0), max 2 decimals Max 2 decimals, 0 is valid trail.points[i].height_m
Difficulty Optional Required: easy, medium, hard, expert trail.difficulty
Activity Type Optional Required: hiking, trail-running, mountain-biking, walking, off-road trail.activity_type
Distance metrics Optional Required, >= 0 trail.total_distance_km, trail.elevation_gain_m, trail.elevation_loss_m
Elevation range Optional min <= max, must match smallest & largest height_m trail.elevation_min_m, trail.elevation_max_m
Point cumulative distance Optional First point 0, monotonically non-decreasing, last equals total_distance_km trail.points[i].distance_km

Frontend Integration Guide

Endpoint

POST /posts/complete-embed

Headers

Header Value Description
Authorization Bearer <JWT_TOKEN> Required
Content-Type multipart/form-data Required

Form Fields (Multipart)

Field Type Required Description
sid string Yes Upload session ID from /posts/init
is_post string Yes Must be "trail"
action string No "draft" (default) or "publish"
description string Yes Post description (1 - 2200 characters)
visibility string No "public" (default), "unlisted", or "private"
location string On Publish JSON string containing place details. location_name is used as the title.
little_planet string Yes Send "false"
animation string Yes Send "false"
trail string Yes Stringified JSON of the trail structure

Example Usage

1. Save Trail Draft

curl -X POST "https://api-post.panorra.com/posts/complete-embed" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>" \
  -F "sid=c943fb9a747-2026100209214600" \
  -F "is_post=trail" \
  -F "action=draft" \
  -F "description=Drafting Mount Pancar scenic hiking route" \
  -F "little_planet=false" \
  -F "animation=false" \
  -F 'trail={
    "points": [
      {
        "url": "https://tourmkr.com/F1a1b2c3",
        "name": "Trailhead",
        "height_m": 725,
        "lat": -6.5806,
        "lng": 106.9005,
        "distance_km": 0
      }
    ]
  }'

Response (HTTP 200 OK)

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Add Post Complete Embed Success",
    "slug": "c943fb9a747-2026100209214600",
    "thumbnail": "https://tourmkr.com/F1a1b2c3"
  }
}

curl -X POST "https://api-post.panorra.com/posts/complete-embed" \
